study_info.title: Vitamin D supplementation improves cytokine profiles in patients with congestive heart failure: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial
study_info.authors: Stefanie S Schleithoff, Armin Zittermann, Gero Tenderich, Heiner K Berthold, Peter Stehle, and Reiner Koerfer
study_info.study_design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. Randomization was performed using computer-generated random number lists.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Ambulatory patients with congestive heart failure, New York Heart Association functional class II.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Hypercalcemia, serum creatinine concentration >2 mg/dL, nephrolithiasis, sarcoidosis, use of a biventricular pacemaker, acute heart insufficiency, and an actual intake of supplements containing vitamin D and calcium.
study_info.study_setting: Heart and Diabetes Center Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany; ambulatory patients routinely seen at least twice a year.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Heart and Diabetes Center Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany
study_info.dropout_reasons: Lack of compliance, worsening health status (including nephrolithiasis, cardiac transplantation, biventricular pacemaker implantation, excessive impairment in health status such as stroke, resuscitation, high hospitalization rate), and death.

minimal_units.intervention_details: 50 micrograms (2000 IU) vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) per day plus 500 mg calcium per day
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: Compliance was documented by controlling the study medication at each visit (bottle counts) and by the analysis of serum 25(OH)D concentrations.

minimal_units.control_details: Placebo (Migliol-Oel) plus 500 mg calcium per day
minimal_units.adherence_to_control: Compliance was documented by controlling the study medication at each visit (bottle counts) and by the analysis of serum 25(OH)D concentrations.

meta_analysis_parameters.outcome_domain: major adverse cardiovascular events；myocardial infarction；stroke or cerebrovascular events；cardiovascular disease mortality；all-cause mortality
